draft.title: Circuits and circuit diagrams
card: An electric circuit is a path that charge can flow around. A complete circuit needs three things: a power source, a closed path of wires, and a load.
a cell or battery. It gives energy to the charge in the circuit.
a device that changes electrical energy into other forms, such as a globe making light and heat.
If the path has a gap, such as an open switch, no current flows and the load does not work. A circuit diagram draws each part with a standard symbol, joined by straight lines for wires.
draft.remember: Source, closed path and load make a circuit. A circuit diagram shows them with symbols.

a.q: A torch has a battery, wires and a globe, but the globe does not light. The switch is open. Why does the globe stay off?
opts: The open switch leaves a gap, so the path is not closed
The battery cannot give energy to the charge in a torch
The globe needs a second load before it can light up
The wires already close the path, so no current is needed
a.why: An open switch breaks the path, so charge cannot flow around and the globe gets no current. The wires alone do not make a working circuit: the path must be closed as well as having a source and a load.
a.clue: Look for a gap in the path.

b.q: Jaya draws a circuit diagram for a buzzer. It shows a cell joined to a buzzer by wires in a closed loop. Which part of her diagram is the load?
b.why: The buzzer changes electrical energy into sound, so it is the load. The cell is the power source. The wires form the path, which is closed as a loop.
b.clue: Which part changes electrical energy into another form?

wants.brief: A circuit diagram with standard symbols: a cell, a switch, a globe and straight wires joined in a closed rectangle. Label the cell 'power source', the globe 'load' and the lines 'wires'.
wants.why: It shows how symbols stand for the real parts of a circuit.

a.best: The open switch leaves a gap, so the path is not closed
